inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: Micheál Martin may point to more tenancies, but that is no comfort to families facing eviction or homelessness. Rising notices and emergency accommodation show that stability—not a flattering headline—is what matters. The six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 may sound reassuring, but more regulation cannot substitute for a housing system that gives families secure homes and owners confidence to provide them. The government should be judged by whether people can remain housed, not by statistics that make insecurity look like progress.
